chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you know how the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) accepted the allegiance of the women?' I said: 'Allah knows best, and the son of His Messenger knows best.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He gathered them around him, then called for a Baram bowl, poured a little water into it, then immersed his hand in it, then said:
ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) accept the pledge of allegiance from women according to Shia sources?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific ritual of bay'ah for women, emphasizing that it was conducted through a verbal contract and the dipping of hands in water rather than the physical handshake common for men, thereby preserving modesty. It underscores the continuity of the covenant made in Surah Al-Murjamlat (60:12) and highlights the Prophet's exceptional purity, noting that his hand was more fragrant than a woman's hand despite not being a mahram, a detail cherished in Shia exegetical tradition.
